name: manual_b1cfec
claim: Meta-instruction, in effect until the v2 oramasys org multi-repo centralization is complete: before pushing a fix to either orama-system or Perpetua-Tools, check whether the same file, or the same underlying concept, exists in the sibling repo and whether it's actually in sync -- not just "did I apply the fix I meant to apply," but "is the BEST version of this fix now present in both repos, chosen by comparing them directly, not by assuming whichever repo I fixed first is automatically correct." Where the two repos' versions differ, the better one (more defensive pattern, more complete investigation notes, more accurate glob/scope) should be adopted in both, not just the one being actively worked on. This bidirectional check is a stopgap for the current two-repo-with-manual-sync architecture; once v2's centralized package/multi-repo structure lands, this class of drift should become structurally impossible rather than something that needs checking by hand every time.

decisions.notes: Explicit meta-instruction from the user, scoped to remain in effect until v2 oramasys org multi-repo centralization removes the need for manual bidirectional sync-checking.

rationale: Explicit meta-instruction from the user, scoped to remain in effect until v2 oramasys org multi-repo centralization removes the need for manual bidirectional sync-checking.
